author: Ben Janca
description: Game Freak's brand-new title: Beast of Reincarnation is an action RPG with a fusion of real-time and turn-based combat. Experience the innovative "one-person, one-dog action RPG" in the beautiful yet harsh world of Beast of Reincarnation. What awaits at the end of Emma and Koo's journey?
title: Beast Of Reincarnation – Official Cinematic Launch Trailer

author: Cheri Faulkner
description:
Beast of Reincarnation is the new action-RPG from Pokemon developer Game Freak, and offers a very different experience from the creature-collecting bliss you're used to. It has three difficulty options, with each being designed so that a wider variety of players can enjoy it, unlike a typical Soulslike game.

Story Mode is best for those who want to play through the narrative without finding combat too challenging. Parry timing is more forgiving, and enemies deal less damage. You'll still need to engage with the combat, but you'll be punished far less for any mistakes you make. If you're playing this for the Game Freak name rather than a passion for a challenging RPG, opt for Story Mode.

Normal Mode is the intended experience, with balanced challenges and normal parry timing. It's intended to encourage you to learn enemy attack patterns, rely on Koo
title: Beast Of Reincarnation Difficulty Options – How To Change Difficulty

author: Jake Dekker
description: Game Freak’s foray into the action-RPG genre lands with mixed results.
title: Beast of Reincarnation Review

author: Cheri Faulkner
description:
It can be pretty daunting stepping foot into a challenging RPG. Beast of Reincarnation is deliberately intended to make you approach it like a Soulslike, so there's no shame in admitting you need some help from time to time. Thanks to Emma and Koo's well-populated skill trees and synergies, there are plenty of approaches you can take, and what may seem like a tall order can be made a little simpler by taking your time, reading the in-game tutorials, and optimizing your build.

With that in mind, we've put together some essential tips for the early game in Beast of Reincarnation, so that you can progress through the story with a little less friction. But not none at all, because that wouldn't be any fun.
title: Beast Of Reincarnation Tips And Beginner’s Guide

author: Jake Dekker
description:
When you start a new game in Game Freak’s Beast of Reincarnation, a prompt asks if you’d like to play in cinematic mode. This locks the cutscene frame rate to 24 frames per second, but, understandably, leaves the gameplay as is. When I first saw this during my 90-minute preview session last month, it felt like a bold statement from Game Freak. Pokemon, Game Freak’s multigenerational smash-hit, can be described as many things, but cinematic it certainly is not. Unfortunately, aside from its flashy combat and a few cutscenes, Beast of Reincarnation isn't really cinematic, either. Flat performances and robotic animations undermine its fascinating story, bland environments sour its beautiful art direction, and an overall lack of polish hampers its intense combat. Though there are aspects of Beast of Reincarnation that I adored, for each one of them there’s always something that holds it back.

Beast of Reincarnation takes p
title: Beast Of Reincarnation’s Cinematic Focus Fails Its Flashy Action

author: Cheri Faulkner
description:
Throughout Beast of Reincarnation, you'll unlock plenty of skills for Emma and Koo, but in the early game that can be a little overwhelming. You'll first need to decide where to invest your attribute points, as some skills and mods are locked until you upgrade the main skill they're nested beneath.

While there are several viable approaches, we think the best way to approach the early game while you're getting to grips with the mechanics is to focus on increasing Emma's AoE damage while leaning on Koo's support abilities. With that in mind, these are the best Beast of Reincarnation skills to focus on unlocking first:

Emma's Best Skills
title: Best Beast Of Reincarnation Skills For The Early Game

author: Reyna Cervantes
description:
Catherine celebrated its 15-year anniversary on July 26, 2026. Below, we examine how this game was an early, if awkward, pioneer in trans representation in video games.

When Catherine released in 2011 it was a step outside of the box for developer Atlus. The RPG powerhouse team wasn't as popular as it is today, and while it had built up a solid reputation from developing the Shin Megami Tensei and Persona series, Atlus had yet to quite break through into mainstream gaming. When the team decided to develop Catherine, it did so with the mindset of exploring more adult themes and identities. Chief among them was one of gaming’s few examples of trans representation. Though the intention of this character was well meaning, cultural divides caused a bit of controversy in the West.

After the long development of Shin Megami Tensei: Persona 4, the team decided to branch out into a w
title: 15 Years Ago, Catherine Had Gaming’s Most Complex Trans Representation

author: Chris Compendio
description:
Praise for something new can often come at the expense of what came before it. One aspect of art and media criticism that I find irksome is that to uplift new works, older ones from the same lineage are often undersold at best, or completely thrown under the bus at worst. It’s a trend I’ve seen most recently with Splatoon Raiders, the first spin-off title in one of my favorite Nintendo franchises.

Splatoon Raiders may very well be the best single-player-focused experience in the series, but let’s not fool ourselves into thinking that the campaigns in Splatoons 1, 2, or 3 were significantly inferior, from either a gameplay or story aspect. In fact, they were pretty damn fresh.
title: Splatoon Raiders Owes A Lot To Older Campaigns You Forgot About

author: Myles Obenza
description: Riftbound, the League of Legends trading card game (TCG) from Riot Games, just saw the release of its fourth expansion Vendetta on July 31, the first set to achieve release parity among all of the game's available languages. We still have one more expansion to come in 2026, with Radiance dropping October 23, but today's State of the Game update detailed even more products play
title: We Got Our First Look at Riftbound’s 2027 Release Lineup

author: Alessandro Barbosa
description:
Halo: Combat Evolved is 25 years old now, so it's a marvel that playing its most recent remake, Halo: Campaign Evolved, is still as fun as it is. Everything from the weight of the weaponry, the ambiance of the Halo installation, the screams of fleeing grunts, and the grin-inducing sound of a plasma grenade exploding on an unfortunate target are all here to remind you (or introduce you) to the most important franchise in Xbox history. It's a series that has struggled in recent times, and it's easy to see this reminder of Halo's roots as critical to its future. So why do I keep wanting to go back to its flawed, latest entry instead?

Halo Infinite was always going to miss the mark in some way. It was a victim of troubled development, responsible for selling a console that struggled out of the gate, and tasked with being both an end to the tired tale from previous entries as well as the start of a wholly new one. Infinite
title: Halo: Campaign Evolved Reminded Me That Halo Infinite Was Great, Actually

author: Myles Obenza
description:
Riftbound, Riot Games' League of Legends trading card game (TCG), recently celebrated its one-year anniversary on August 1 during GenCon. Since its launch late last year, the game's undergone dozens of changes, errata, rules updates, and even card bans. In its first of three State of the Game updates this week (and second overall this year), Riot broke down some of the biggest changes coming to Riftbound starting in January of 2027 with the release of the game's sixth set, Legacy.

Two State of the Game update articles were released today on Riot's site. One was an
title: Riftbound’s Card Templates Are Getting A Big Overhaul in 2027

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
The Palworld series is expanding. Garena has announced Palworld Online, a new MMORPG for mobile, which the developer is making under a licensing deal with Palworld developer Pocketpair.

Garena will develop and publish Palworld Online for iOS and Android. The game aims to reimagine the "depth, freedom, and scale" of the main game for mobile. Palworld Online will have new, original story elements, along with MMO features like a "seamless, interconnected open world," Garena said. The game has cooperative and competitive elements, just like the main game does.
title: A New Palworld Game Has Been Announced, And It’s Releasing Pretty Soon

author: Alessandro Barbosa
description:
Hold on tight to the graphics cards you have, because those sitting on retailer shelves are about to get a lot more expensive, irrespective of whether you prefer AMD or Nvidia.

Last week, Nvidia GPUs were confirmed to be getting a substantial price hike, with anything between 20% and 30% being reported. That gave AMD the perfect moment to communicate a price increase of its own, with market analyst Harukaze571 reporting that the company had been waiting for Nvidia to make the first move.

The report, via PC Gamer, suggests that AMD was planning its own GPU price hike, but was worried about it
title: No Matter Which You Choose, Graphics Cards Are About To Get A Lot More Expensive

author: Blair Marnell
description:
When Baldur's Gate 3 launched in 2023, it didn't take long for modders to add new camera options, including a third-person view. Now, a new third-person mod is expanding the view of Baldur's Gate 3 and allowing veteran players a chance to revisit the game from a fresh perspective.

The true third-person mod was created and posted by Nexus mods user Relysia, who acknowledges that it builds upon the previously released native camera tweeks mod and retains its features. However, the new mod adds a way to toggle between an over-the-shoulder camera view and
title: Baldur’s Gate 3 Third-Person Mod Revitalizes The Game

author: Callum Self
description:
As someone who has stopped playing Lego games in recent years-not because I've lost my childhood innocence, but because I simply haven't enjoyed them-Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight feels like a blueprint for the future of the brick-building franchise. It's fun for kids and adults alike, and almost every joke lands in a way that few games have managed for me in years. The last time I remember laughing this much at a Lego game was Darth Maul's appearance, where multiple lightsaber blades shot out in the silliest way possible. It's an experience I highly recommend, even if you're an adult, and the chance to get it for just $1 is difficult to pass up.

If you're looking to get Lego Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight for just $1, here's your chance. The
title: Here’s Your Chance To Get Lego Batman: Legacy Of the Dark Knight For Just $1

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
It's time for another sale on PC games, and this time, you can strap in for Steam Cyberpunk Fest 2026, which shines a light on the games that celebrate the future and the inevitable dystopia we're headed towards. Constant surveillance, corporations becoming national powers, and neon lighting are hallmarks of the genre, and plenty of games have dipped their toes into that dark future. With so much to choose from, where does one even begin?

We've taken a look at the games on sale and dropped some of our picks below for a mix of hard-hitting futurism and atmospheric worldbuilding, all spread across various genres.

As a reminder, Steam Cyberpunk Fest runs August 3-10, and once it concludes, it'll be followed by Pins & Pegs Fest (August 17-20) and PvE Survival Crafting Fest (August 31 - September 7). For a closer look at what the rest of the year holds in store--as well as the first
title: Steam Cyberpunk Fest Is Full Of Hidden Gems And Modern Classics

author: Vic Hood
description:
Phasmophobia is full of spooky, funny, and downright weird easter eggs that ghost hunters should keep an eye out for. From props that reference classic horror movies like The Ring and Friday the 13th to hidden pieces of lore and nods to popular Phasmophobia streamers, there are plenty of secrets for eagle-eyed players to uncover on select maps. After all, ghost hunting doesn’t have to be scary all of the time.

While finding many of these secrets offers you nothing but sheer joy, there are two main map easter eggs that present you with a series of head-scratching puzzles. However, if you manage to solve them, you’re rewarded with a special ID Card and Badge. So, below, we break down all the hidden references and secrets to look out for in Phasmophobia, and how to solve the Point Hope and Nell’s Diner easter eggs so you can claim your nifty prizes.
title: All Phasmophobia Easter Eggs And Secrets

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Buying a new Xbox just got a lot more expensive in the US, Europe, and UK. The previously announced Xbox Series X|S price hikes are now in effect as of August 1, and people should expect to pay significantly more.

In the US, all 512GB Xbox models went up by $100, while the 1 TB systems are now $150 more expensive. All 2 TB models are discontinued. You can see all the new US prices below, and prices for other regions further down (via VGC).

  • Xbox Series S 512GB - $500
  • Xbox Series S 1TB - $600
  • Xbox Series X 1TB digital edition - $750
title: Xbox Price Hikes Are Now In Effect Worldwide

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description: Love and Deepspace just had its worst financial month to date, as the dating gacha sim's revenue has cratered. While it was pulling in around $30 - $60 million in revenue every month (per Sensor Data), July saw the game make a noticeably smaller amount of cash, to the tune of $10.3 million. That's a massive 73% drop when compared to June 2026 ($38 million), and the fall can all be traced back to the announcement--and
title: Love And Deepspace’s Biggest Controversy Is Now Hitting Its Wallet

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
An 18-year-old from New Hampshire released a game called This Game Costs $200 earlier this year as a joke--but a lot of people bought it. The game generated $1.3 million in sales, but creator Michael Major didn't get anywhere near that big of a payday.

He told WMUR that he set the price at $200 because that was the maximum a game could be listed for on Steam, and he expected no one to buy it. When he saw revenue of $1.3 million, he "almost died," Major said. To be sure, there are games on Steam that cost more than $200--
title: Viral Steam Game Made $1.3 Million But Creator Only Got $2,000 After Mass Refunds

author: Erick Tay
description: In a world run by demons, you're still stuck at your office job in this upcoming horror game.
title: HR: Human Remains Exclusive Release Date Trailer

author: Mark Delaney
description:
A famous poet once said, "Work sucks; I know." That timeless truth is the backdrop for HR: Human Remains, an upcoming first-person horror game in which demons have taken over the world, but you're still clocking in for your desk job. 

Today, GameSpot can exclusively reveal the release date; it's coming to Steam on September 22. Check out the brand-new release date trailer below for more.

With an aesthetic reminiscent of the original PlayStation era, HR: Human Remains has a darkly humorous tone, but is still very much a horror game.

In it, you'll be stuck as an office clerk, interacting with co-workers and your extra-horrible bosses while uncovering a story with multiple endings to experience based on your choices.
title: The World’s Gone To Hell, But You Still Have To Go To Work, Just Like In This Horror Game

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
A new Nintendo Direct has been announced, and this time, the focus is on Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave. If you're interested, you can tune in at 7 AM PT / 10 AM ET on August 4 to watch the broadcast. Nintendo says that you can expect "roughly 20 minutes" of new information about the game.

One of several big first-party games from Nintendo scheduled for launch this year, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave is the first game in the longrunning tactical-RPG series to be developed exclusively for Switch 2 consoles. The last time it was in the spotlight was during the June Nintendo Direct, where a few more details about the game were revealed.

The game will feature four characters
title: Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave Nintendo Direct Announced For This Week

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Marvel's Wolverine is finally slashing its way onto PS5 next month, and ahead of its release, it looks like the game is going to earn its Mature 17+ rating with blood and ass. According to the Entertainment Software Rating Board, the game contains blood, gore, drug references, strong language, and "partial nudity," but it's not specified whose gluteus maximus is on display.

"A handful of sequences briefly depict a character's exposed buttocks," the ESRB rating reads. That's a pretty vague description, but we'd wager that we could see Wolverine's butt paraded about, given the character's habit of being occasionally transformed into a naked and feral mutant weapon by shadowy organizations like Canada's Department H.
title: Marvel’s Wolverine Might Be Continuing Hugh Jackman’s Infamous Bare Butt Tradition

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Bruce Straley, the Naughty Dog veteran who worked on the Jak, Uncharted, and The Last of Us franchises before leaving to start his own studio, is asking his followers why they are excited for GTA 6.

Posting on social media, Straley said he's asking this question out of genuine curiosity, and not simply to stir the pot. "No shade, just curious," he said.

Straley said he's unsure if he's interested in playing GTA 6, so he was asking followers to share the reasons why they are excited for Rockstar's next big game.

"What do you hope is new in GTA 6 you haven’t already experienced in its predecessors? OR simply, Why are you gonna play GTA 6?
title: The Last Of Us Co-Director Asks Why You Even Care About GTA 6, And The Internet Has Thoughts

author: Eddie Makuch
description:
Inde Navarrette reached a new level of fame this year after starring in Curry Barker's horror movie Obsession. She's also a big fan of video games. She's now revealed that she's been offered roles in games, and that she loves Shrek.

"Yes, and I'm starting my journey with that soon," she told Variety when asked if any studios had come calling to ask her to be in a video game. "I want to try something smaller to test the waters and then later, different. Video games are, obviously, a big interest of mine."

She is a big fan of Resident Evil, adding that she would "die inside" if she got the chance to have a role in one of the games someday.

Navarrette did not name the companies that have pitched
title: Obsession Star Inde Navarrette Has Been Offered Video Game Roles, Loves Shrek

author: Mark Delaney
description:
In the three years since Big Walk was announced, I've heard it referred to as a co-op walking sim, a puzzle-adventure game, and friendslop. After spending 20+ hours in the world of the Australian Outback-inspired game, it's no easier to succinctly define it, because it's not actually like anything else. By inventively stripping down the medium to its most essential parts, it invites novices and experts alike to build it back up from scratch, coloring in its mysterious world with their friends by their side. We need a new word for whatever kind of game Big Walk really is, but here's one for now: unforgettable. 

Big Walk is a game about walking and talking with friends, played in first-person for groups of 2-12 players. Embodying vaguely humanoid characters--think multicolored snowmen with long noses and noodly appendages--you and y
title: Big Walk Is One Of The Best Co-Op Games Ever

author: Richard Li
description: House House's follow-up to Untitled Goose Game is a singularly special adventure.
title: Big Walk Is The Best Co-Op Game I’ve Played In A Long Time – Review

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Summerslam weekend saw several new champions emerge, but Cody Rhodes wasn't one of them. While the American Nightmare failed in his bid to dethrone CM Punk as the WWE Undisputed Champion, at least he managed to turn heads with his ring outfit, which went all in with Street Fighter influences. Rhodes--who plays Guile in the upcoming Street Fighter movie--hit the ring with a mask that captured the absurdity of Guile's signature hairdo and M. Bison's Shadaloo organization.

Given that the Street Fighter film was one of Summerslam's sponsors, it wasn't too surprising to see Rhodes geared up to help promote the upcoming movie. Just before he appeared, the PPV featured a character select screen in the same style as Street Fighter 2, with WWE performers like S
title: Cody Rhodes Went Full Street Fighter For SummerSlam

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day came out swinging at the box office on the weekend, as the new Spidey movie took in a Hulk-sized $927 million at the global box office. In the US, the domestic box office take clocked in at an impressive $355 million, which works out to 38.3% of the opening weekend haul.

Once again starring Tom Holland as the webhead, Spider-Man: Brand New Day earned the biggest opening of the year so far--and by a comfortable margin when compared to other 2026 blockbusters like The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. In the US, it opened in 4,487 theaters. It's a big start to the first Spider-Man movie since 2021's No Way Home, but Brand New Day was a few million short of breaking the record set by 2019's Avengers: Endgame, which opened to $357 mi
title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Wins Over Hideo Kojima, Then Conquers The Box Office
